question: Why can knowledge distillation be useful in self-supervised vision methods like DINO?
direct_answer: It turns teacher-student consistency into a label-free learning signal that shapes strong visual representations.
expanded_answer: Self-supervised distillation lets the model learn from consistency across augmented views without any manual labels. A teacher can produce a target for one view, and the student must predict that target from another view, which encourages invariance to viewpoint and augmentation while preserving semantic structure. This makes distillation a core mechanism for modern self-supervised representation learning.
key_points: Learns semantic structure from augmentation consistency
common_wrong_ideas: Distillation is only a compression trick
Self-supervised distillation cannot learn meaningful features
